comments-el26-67-spartz.point: She asks for a moratorium on discretionary approvals for new and pending large-load projects until reliability, cost and transparency safeguards exist.
comments-el26-67-spartz.quote: suspend or condition discretionary approvals affecting new and pending major data centers, cryptocurrency mining operations, and associated infrastructure until essential reliability, cost-allocation, transparency, and financial safeguards are established.

comments-el26-67-spartz.point: She seeks a national inventory of existing and proposed large loads, including beneficial owners and potential stranded costs.
comments-el26-67-spartz.quote: Establish a transparent national accounting of proposed and existing major electricity loads, identifying developers, beneficial owners, affiliates, verified demand, financial commitments

comments-el26-67-spartz.point: Large-load developers should bear incremental generation and transmission costs, with review of deposits, guarantees, minimum payments and termination fees.
comments-el26-67-spartz.quote: Review deposits, financial guarantees, minimum-payment obligations, termination fees, and protections against stranded costs.

comments-el26-67-spartz.point: She asks for an independent review of PJM and MISO governance that cites docket EL26-67-000.
comments-el26-67-spartz.quote: FERC Docket EL26-67-000: Preliminary findings concerning potentially unjust, unreasonable, or discriminatory large-load interconnection rules.

comments-el26-67-spartz.point: She requests separate written responses from FERC and DOE within 30 days and a corrective-action report within 90 days.
comments-el26-67-spartz.quote: I request separate written responses from FERC and DOE within 30 days identifying:

filing-20260807-5219.point: CEBA supports a 90-day abeyance because it lets stakeholders work with PJM rather than shift debate to the Commission docket.
filing-20260807-5219.quote: Granting the requested abeyance will promote administrative efficiencies by allowing time for PJM and stakeholders—including CEBA and its members—to work collaboratively

filing-20260807-5219.point: CEBA says 90 days would not materially impede FERC's goals and supports commercial viability and legal durability of the mid-November filings.
filing-20260807-5219.quote: a 90-day extension would not materially impede the Commission’s objectives for advancing reforms quickly

filing-20260804-5159.point: Constellation says it responds only to the clarification request and calls the rehearing arguments premature.
filing-20260804-5159.quote: Exelon and FirstEnergy’s arguments are premature and barred by Rule 713 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure.

filing-20260804-5159.point: It calls the Point of Change in Ownership request a collateral attack on prior FERC rulings in the co-location dockets.
filing-20260804-5159.quote: This request for clarification is a thinly-veiled collateral attack on the Commission’s previous rulings in Docket Numbers ER26- 1088-000 and ER26-1479-000.

filing-20260804-5159.point: It asks FERC to clarify that eligibility requirements must not be so prescriptive that they disqualify large loads.
filing-20260804-5159.quote: any eligibility requirements PJM and the Transmission Owners propose in their initial filings must not be so prescriptive as to improperly disqualify large loads

filing-20260804-5159.point: It also asks that no reference point be used to define electrically proximate large load in a way that undermines speedy interconnection.
filing-20260804-5159.quote: may not use the Point of Change in Ownership, or any other point of reference, to define “electrically proximate large load” in a manner that likewise undermines speedy interconnection

filing-20260803-5234.point: Constellation supports abeyance on the condition that PJM still files a complete set of Interim NITS provisions on August 17, 2026.
filing-20260803-5234.quote: PJM remains obligated to file on August 17, 2026, a complete set of provisions to facilitate Interim Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”), that will allow for a prompt start of service.

filing-20260803-5234.point: Constellation says Contract Demand Services may need up to 90 more days while Interim NITS is basically NITS.
filing-20260803-5234.quote: developing the terms and conditions for Contract Demand Services may require an additional 90 days.

filing-20260803-5234.point: It asks FERC to require PJM to reconsider its proposed June 1, 2029 Interim NITS effective date.
filing-20260803-5234.quote: Reconsider its proposed June 1, 2029 effective date given that the interconnection of large loads is an “urgent” issue

filing-20260803-5234.point: Constellation says the two proceedings have distinct compliance obligations that PJM must not conflate.
filing-20260803-5234.quote: they are separate proceedings with distinct compliance obligations that PJM must not conflate

filing-20260803-5106.point: The Coalition agrees with PJM's coordinated approach to the two dockets, which would produce filings by mid-November.
filing-20260803-5106.quote: PJMICC agrees with PJM’s proposed approach, which facilitates administrative efficiencies and helps consolidate stakeholder and party resources and work efforts.

filing-20260803-5106.point: It calls 90 days proportionate, though potentially still an aggressive timeline.
filing-20260803-5106.quote: Even a 90-day extension is still potentially an aggressive timeline, but it better strikes the balance between the FERC’s urgent call for reforms and the need for time to create a durable compliance filing.

filing-20260803-5106.point: It also supports the Indicated Transmission Owners' parallel requests running to November 16, 2026.
filing-20260803-5106.quote: PJMICC also supports the requests of the Indicated Transmission Owners for extension and abeyance, respectively, until November 16, 2026.

filing-20260803-5261.point: Silver Run asks for a 90-day full abeyance to coordinate with PJM and prepare a section 205 filing.
filing-20260803-5261.quote: Silver Run seeks a 90-day full abeyance of the current 60-day deadline to respond to all issues raised in the Show Cause Order

filing-20260803-5261.point: It expects revisions on large load definition, readiness requirements, alternative transmission technology evaluation and a pro forma service agreement.
filing-20260803-5261.quote: the definition of a large load; readiness and information requirements; the evaluation of alternative transmission technologies; a pro forma service agreement memorializing operational terms

filing-20260803-5261.point: It expects cost recovery, financial security and rate provisions to mitigate cost shifting, and a reasonable implementation period.
filing-20260803-5261.quote: cost recovery, associated financial security, and rate treatment provisions intended to mitigate cost shifting among transmission customers

filing-20260803-5261.point: Silver Run says its filing depends on PJM's stakeholder process because it runs none of its own.
filing-20260803-5261.quote: Silver Run does not administer a stakeholder process of its own through which the issues raised in the Show Cause Order could be resolved independently.

filing-20260728-5071.point: The Transmission Owners ask for a 90-day abeyance to November 16, 2026 to develop section 205 filings.
filing-20260728-5071.quote: respectfully move to hold the deadline to respond in the above- captioned proceeding in abeyance for 90 days, until November 16, 2026.

filing-20260728-5071.point: They expect to file a pro forma cost recovery agreement and rates for flexible and electrically proximate large load services, with penalties for exceeding contractual limits.
filing-20260728-5071.quote: will contain a pro forma cost recovery agreement(s), as well as rates for new transmission services for “flexible large loads” and “electrically proximate large loads or co-located loads.”

filing-20260728-5071.point: They say a cost recovery agreement raises open issues, including overlap with bilateral retail agreements and how to set each customer's minimum contribution.
filing-20260728-5071.quote: the specific mechanism for determining each Eligible Customer’s required minimum contribution.

filing-20260728-5071.point: They may revise local planning procedures such as Attachment M-3 to meet the order's transparency findings on Network Upgrade costs.
filing-20260728-5071.quote: considering what, if any, PJM Tariff modifications they will need to include in their own FPA section 205 filing(s) relating to transparency enhancements.

filing-20260728-5071.point: They ask FERC to rule by August 10 with a five-day comment period.
filing-20260728-5071.quote: request that the Commission establish a comment period of five (5) days.

motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.point: PJM seeks a 90-day abeyance because the show cause reforms build on co-located load compliance changes.
motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.quote: Many of the changes contemplated in the Large Load Order will build upon compliance changes recently ordered for Co-Located Load in Docket Nos. EL25-49-000, et al.

motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.point: PJM expects its section 205 filing in early to mid-November.
motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.quote: PJM anticipates submitting that filing by early to mid-November.

motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.point: The overlap covers expanded transmission services, study procedures and operational requirements.
motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.quote: (1) expansion of new transmission services; (2) study procedures; and (3) operational requirements.

motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.point: PJM's planned filing covers study processes with alternative transmission technologies, cost shifting and transparency, flexible load services, and proximate generation study.
motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.quote: achieve efficient transmission service application and study processes, including through the consideration of alternative transmission technologies

motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.point: PJM schedules stakeholder sessions on July 30, August 18 and September 16, with an advisory vote on October 28, 2026.
motion-el26-67-pjm-abeyance.quote: with the goal of taking an advisory stakeholder vote on the proposal at the meeting of the Members Committee on October 28, 2026

filing-20260728-5074.point: Wabash says it ceased to be a public utility on January 1, 2025 because it is wholly owned by exempt cooperatives.
filing-20260728-5074.quote: January 1, 2025 because it became exempt from the Federal Power Act as a result of being wholly owned by exempt entities.

filing-20260728-5074.point: Wabash says it is similarly situated to the non-jurisdictional owners FERC listed in footnote 13.
filing-20260728-5074.quote: it is a PTO that is similarly situated to all of the other non-jurisdictional entities listed in footnote 13 of the Order.

filing-20260728-5074.point: Wabash does not dispute the need to address large-load and co-located load service in organized markets.
filing-20260728-5074.quote: it does not dispute the need for the Commission to address issues surrounding service to large load and co-located load within organized markets and elsewhere.

filing-20260728-5074.point: The requested errata would remove Wabash from the caption and add it to footnote 13.
filing-20260728-5074.quote: removes WVPA from the caption of Docket No. EL26-67-000, which intended to identify only PJM and jurisdictional PTOs

filing-20260722-5175.point: Allegheny says it is owned by its members and is not a public utility subject to FERC jurisdiction.
filing-20260722-5175.quote: Allegheny is not a public utility subject to FERC jurisdiction, pursuant to Section 201(f) of the Federal Power Act.

filing-20260722-5175.point: FERC exempted other non-public-utility owners from the order while keeping authority over their tariff provisions through PJM.
filing-20260722-5175.quote: it retains the authority to review each of these entities’ tariff provisions as a component of PJM’s Tariff in an order to show cause directed towards PJM

filing-20260722-5175.point: Allegheny cites the CAISO order's offer to rescind at a non-public utility's request and notes its PJM tariff portions contain no interconnection processes.
filing-20260722-5175.quote: we will rescind the show cause order against them at their request

filing-20260722-5175.point: Allegheny asks for rescission and a waiver of notice and comment periods.
filing-20260722-5175.quote: respectfully requests that the Commission rescind the PJM Show Cause Order against it, as a non-public utility

filing-20260720-5172.point: Exelon and FirstEnergy challenge the finding that PJM's tariff lacks services for flexible large loads, calling it arbitrary and not reasoned.
filing-20260720-5172.quote: The Commission’s findings that the PJM Tariff appears to be unjust and unreasonable without these new transmission service options is arbitrary and capricious and not based upon reasoned decision making.

filing-20260720-5172.point: They say the new services would only cut transmission charges for large loads at other customers' expense.
filing-20260720-5172.quote: the creation of these new forms of transmission service will not hasten or improve service and instead merely reduce transmission charges for large loads at the expense of other customers.

filing-20260720-5172.point: They say FERC's burden under section 206 is unmet because the record shows no inability to get service under existing Network Service.
filing-20260720-5172.quote: There is No Evidence In the Record That Flexible Large Loads or Any Other Large Loads Are Unable to Obtain Reliable, Timely, and Reasonably Priced Service Using the Existing Network Service Construct.

filing-20260720-5172.point: They say large loads rely on the whole embedded system, so embedded costs should be charged for their full gross load.
filing-20260720-5172.quote: Flexible Large Loads and Other Large Loads Rely Upon the Entire Embedded Transmission System to Serve Their Full Gross Load.

filing-20260720-5172.point: They argue the new services intrude on state retail authority.
filing-20260720-5172.quote: FERC’s CD Services similarly interfere with States’ regulation of the terms of sale at retail

filing-20260720-5198.point: The Transmission Owners say the 50 MW definition should not prevent added criteria for the services the order contemplates.
filing-20260720-5198.quote: does not limit PJM or the PJM Transmission Owners from proposing additional criteria or reasonable distinctions between large load customers for purposes of designing and implementing the products addressed in the Order.

filing-20260720-5198.point: They warn a one-size-fits-all approach would be over-inclusive and undermine speed-to-power, repeating the inflated generation queue problem.
filing-20260720-5198.quote: an overly inclusive definition of “large load” risks repeating the same flaws that occurred with inflated generation interconnection queues.

filing-20260720-5198.point: They cite hyperscale computational load versus traditional customers as a distinction that may justify differently designed and priced products.
filing-20260720-5198.quote: functional distinctions between types of customers (e.g., hyperscale computational loads versus “traditional” manufacturing and commercial customers) may merit distinctions in how different products are designed, offered and priced.

filing-20260720-5198.point: They ask to define large and electrically proximate load by reference points other than the point of interconnection, such as Point of Change of Ownership.
filing-20260720-5198.quote: they will have sufficient flexibility to propose other points of reference, such as the Point of Change of Ownership.

filing-20260720-5198.point: They say they are not asking FERC to pick the criterion now, only to keep the point of interconnection from being required.
filing-20260720-5198.quote: the PJM Transmission Owners are not asking the Commission to decide at this time in this proceeding whether the point of interconnection or some other criteria should be used

report-el26-67-pjm.point: PJM points to a Critical Issue Fast Path on backstop procurement as its most direct effort on adequacy for new large loads.
report-el26-67-pjm.quote: this effort is most directly evidenced by the Critical Issue Fast Path (“CIFP”) for the development of a reliability backstop procurement (“RBP”) and a framework for service during periods of insufficient resource adequacy.

report-el26-67-pjm.point: Stakeholders considered 24 proposals, 11 on service during insufficient adequacy and 13 on the backstop, with a filing expected around July 31, 2026.
report-el26-67-pjm.quote: In total, 24 proposals were submitted for consideration by PJM, the Independent Market Monitor for PJM, and various stakeholder groups.

report-el26-67-pjm.point: Large loads that bring too little supply may be required to reduce withdrawals before other load is curtailed.
report-el26-67-pjm.quote: these large loads may be required to reduce their withdrawals from the transmission system before PJM needs to curtail other load.

report-el26-67-pjm.point: A large load flexibility initiative would let loads connect before transmission upgrades, using load-reduction allocations and temporary options.
report-el26-67-pjm.quote: develop options for temporary flexibility to offer loads until transmission upgrades are constructed, such as fully, partially, or storage matched options.

report-el26-67-pjm.point: PJM's Powering Reliability Through Market Design report sets out three paths, with a filing expected in 2027.
report-el26-67-pjm.quote: culminating in a filing with the Commission in 2027.

report-el26-67-pjm.point: PJM reports 829 Cycle 1 applications totaling about 212,000 MW under review.
report-el26-67-pjm.quote: PJM has received a total of 829 applications under Cycle 1, totaling approximately 212,000 MWs of new capacity currently under review.

filing-20260717-5258.point: The Joint Consumer Advocates say the cost shifts come from the PJM Tariff, which only FERC can reform, not from retail rates.
filing-20260717-5258.quote: the cost shifts identified by the Order do not originate at the retail level, and the responsibility to cure them cannot lie with state regulators.

filing-20260717-5258.point: They challenge FERC's reliance on state sub-allocation, since a state cannot move costs between transmission customers under the tariff.
filing-20260717-5258.quote: The PJM Tariff fixes the charges each transmission customer pays, and a state cannot move costs from one transmission customer to another.

filing-20260717-5258.point: They ask FERC to set the standard that a cost recovery agreement is just and reasonable only if the Eligible Customer pays the full Network Upgrade cost.
filing-20260717-5258.quote: An agreement is just and reasonable only if it requires the Eligible Customer to pay the full cost of the Network Upgrades needed to accommodate the large load.

filing-20260717-5258.point: Their hypothetical shows a NITS-based agreement paying $21 million in year one against a $36 million revenue requirement increase, a $15 million shortfall.
filing-20260717-5258.quote: That falls $15 million short of the $36 million increase in the annual zonal revenue requirement caused by the Network Upgrades the transmission owner identified

filing-20260717-5258.point: They ask that transmission owners immediately credit cost recovery agreement revenue to other customers in the zone.
filing-20260717-5258.quote: transmission owners must immediately credit all revenue received under cost-recovery agreements to transmission customers in the relevant zone.

filing-20260717-5246.point: OCA says the proposed cost recovery agreements secure revenue under existing allocation methods and do not fix cost shifts to customers not serving large loads.
filing-20260717-5246.quote: Agreements guaranteeing the collection of a revenue contribution from Eligible Customers for Network Upgrades needed to serve large loads is untethered from review or consideration of the actual cost of providing transmission service induced by individual large loads.

filing-20260717-5246.point: OCA reads paragraph 81 as ambiguous on whether parties may build a record on existing regional cost allocation methods.
filing-20260717-5246.quote: Order creates ambiguity whether parties can develop an actionable record on PJM’s wholesale cost allocation methods for Network Upgrades caused by large loads.

filing-20260717-5246.point: Commissioner Chang's concurrence is quoted for the point that revenue contributions untethered from actual cost may not protect other customers.
filing-20260717-5246.quote: bilateral agreements that simply provide transmission revenue contributions untethered from any assessment of the actual cost of providing transmission service induced by individual large loads may be insufficient to adequately protect other customers against unjustified cost shifts.

filing-20260717-5246.point: Seven multi-state PJM zones carry 52 percent of peak load, so state retail sub-allocation cannot undo cost shifts across them.
filing-20260717-5246.quote: These seven multi-state Zones comprise 52 percent of PJM’s peak load.

filing-20260717-5246.point: For regional facilities, PJM splits zonal cost responsibility 50/50 between load factor and distribution factor.
filing-20260717-5246.quote: using a hybrid methodology involving a 50/50 split of each zone’s load factor and distribution factor (DFAX).

filing-20260709-5287.point: New Era says PJM should study a load paired with dependable nearby generation by its enforceable maximum net withdrawal rather than full gross demand.
filing-20260709-5287.quote: PJM should evaluate the project based on the facility’s enforceable maximum net withdrawal from the transmission system, rather than assuming the facility will impose its full gross demand

filing-20260709-5287.point: A net-withdrawal cap would need metering, controls, operator visibility and tariff consequences for exceedance.
filing-20260709-5287.quote: a binding net-withdrawal cap in the relevant service agreement or other tariff- governed arrangement

filing-20260709-5287.point: PJM should say what transmission service an Eligible Customer takes for a load operated under such a cap.
filing-20260709-5287.quote: PJM should also explain what transmission service the Eligible Customer must take for a large load operated subject to an enforceable Maximum Net Withdrawal.

filing-20260709-5287.point: The 30-day adequacy report should cover expedited study of low-risk uprates at existing plants.
filing-20260709-5287.quote: PJM should address whether its Tariff provides an adequate pathway for expedited treatment of uprates at existing generating facilities.

filing-20260709-5287.point: It also asks about expedited reconnection of retired or mothballed capacity without bypassing reliability review.
filing-20260709-5287.quote: The purpose would not be to bypass reliability review, but to avoid subjecting bounded reactivations of existing capacity to procedures designed for wholly new speculative projects.

filing-20260708-5011.point: Maven rates PJM's posture Conditional with two keystone flags, Ratepayer Protection and Financial Surety, which it says warrant Commission intervention.
filing-20260708-5011.quote: PJM's current tariff posture on large-load interconnection scores CONDITIONAL under the Civic Bankability Rating Standard with two active keystone flags

filing-20260708-5011.point: Maven cites the 2027/28 auction as the first to miss the reliability requirement, 6,516.6 MW UCAP short at a 14.4% reserve margin.
filing-20260708-5011.quote: which PJM reported as 6,516.6 MW UCAP below the RTO Reliability Requirement.

filing-20260708-5011.point: Maven says large-load study processes lack a bounded time-to-service commitment or public reporting of completion times.
filing-20260708-5011.quote: proceed without a bounded time-to-service commitment, without public reporting on median or 90th-percentile completion timelines, and without a customer-facing remedy mechanism for delayed studies.

filing-20260708-5011.point: Recommendation 2 asks that upgrade and capacity costs caused by large loads go to the responsible load class, with per-upgrade disclosure.
filing-20260708-5011.quote: attributes transmission upgrade costs and capacity procurement costs caused by large-load interconnection to the responsible load class, not to Load Serving Entities or residential rate classes

filing-20260708-5011.point: Recommendation 4 asks for flexible large-load tariff classes with defined compensation, reliability crediting and financial surety.
filing-20260708-5011.quote: provide for curtailable or interruptible service with defined compensation; (ii) include contribution-to-reliability crediting

filing-20260708-5011.point: Maven says this is one of six coordinated comments across dockets EL26-67 through EL26-72.
filing-20260708-5011.quote: These Comments are one of six substantive Comments Maven files this cycle across the six Show Cause dockets initiated on June 18, 2026 (EL26-67 through EL26-72).

filing-20260708-5012.point: Maven rates PJM's posture Conditional with two keystone flags, Ratepayer Protection and Financial Surety, which it says warrant Commission intervention.
filing-20260708-5012.quote: PJM's current tariff posture on large-load interconnection scores CONDITIONAL under the Civic Bankability Rating Standard with two active keystone flags

filing-20260708-5012.point: Maven cites the 2027/28 auction as the first to miss the reliability requirement, 6,516.6 MW UCAP short at a 14.4% reserve margin.
filing-20260708-5012.quote: which PJM reported as 6,516.6 MW UCAP below the RTO Reliability Requirement.

filing-20260708-5012.point: Maven says large-load study processes lack a bounded time-to-service commitment or public reporting of completion times.
filing-20260708-5012.quote: proceed without a bounded time-to-service commitment, without public reporting on median or 90th-percentile completion timelines, and without a customer-facing remedy mechanism for delayed studies.

filing-20260708-5012.point: Recommendation 2 asks that upgrade and capacity costs caused by large loads go to the responsible load class, with per-upgrade disclosure.
filing-20260708-5012.quote: attributes transmission upgrade costs and capacity procurement costs caused by large-load interconnection to the responsible load class, not to Load Serving Entities or residential rate classes

filing-20260708-5012.point: Recommendation 4 asks for flexible large-load tariff classes with defined compensation, reliability crediting and financial surety.
filing-20260708-5012.quote: provide for curtailable or interruptible service with defined compensation; (ii) include contribution-to-reliability crediting

filing-20260708-5012.point: Maven says this is one of six coordinated comments across dockets EL26-67 through EL26-72.
filing-20260708-5012.quote: These Comments are one of six substantive Comments Maven files this cycle across the six Show Cause dockets initiated on June 18, 2026 (EL26-67 through EL26-72).
